A bridge inspection crew records two kinds of measurements for each cable. The handheld gauge reports tension in kilonewtons at the moment of inspection. The office spreadsheet records the date when a supervisor transcribes the gauge sheet. The transcription date can be several days after the physical measurement. On Tuesday the crew measured cable amber at 342 kilonewtons and cable cobalt at 355 kilonewtons. Both readings were signed on the same paper sheet before the crew left the bridge. A supervisor entered cobalt into the spreadsheet on Wednesday but entered amber on Friday because amber's row needed a spelling correction in its location label. A later reviewer sorted the spreadsheet by entry date and described the cobalt measurement as the older physical reading. The crew log contradicts that description: it has one signed inspection date for both readings, with the two gauge values next to the cable labels. No gauge was recalibrated between the two measurements, and the paper sheet has not been amended. The reviewer needs to state which reading is larger and whether the entry order proves that either measurement happened on an earlier day. Answer in one sentence.
Answer:
cases.continuation: cobalt has the larger tension reading, and spreadsheet entry order does not establish an earlier measurement day.

cases.prompt:
A seed bank tracks sample jars with a shelf ledger and a shipping manifest. Staff assign a permanent accession code when a jar arrives. A manifest number is assigned only if part of the sample is later shipped to another laboratory. Jar maple arrived first and received accession 501. Jar pine arrived next and received accession 502. The bank kept both jars sealed in the same climate-controlled room. On a later afternoon the staff prepared a shipment from pine and printed manifest 88. The following morning they prepared a shipment from maple and printed manifest 89. A visiting researcher saw the lower manifest number on pine and assumed pine had entered the seed bank before maple. The intake ledger, however, is signed at each arrival and lists maple before pine. The researcher also checked that accession codes were not recycled and that neither jar had been returned and readmitted. The shipping clerk explained that manifest numbers track outbound packages, not intake order, and that packages can be prepared in a different sequence from accession. The bank asks for a short clarification that preserves both facts: intake order and outbound paperwork order. State which jar arrived first and which jar was shipped first, naming the record that supports each claim.
Answer:
cases.continuation: maple arrived first according to the accession ledger; pine was shipped first according to the shipping manifests.
